learning_outcomes.text: Be able to prepare technical reports in the field of maintenance of structures and constructions.
Be able to organize teamwork in the preparation of diagnostic reports and proposals for intervention techniques for industrial structures and constructions within an established timeframe.
Be able to apply the dynamic equilibrium equations that govern the behavior of structures under external excitations in specific cases.
Be able to explain the need for intervention in structural and constructive elements as well as the techniques and diagnostic methods.
Be able to formulate the dynamic equilibrium equations that govern the behavior of structures under external excitations.
Be able to detect and diagnose pathological states in structural and constructive elements.
Be able to describe the different techniques of action and conservation in structures and constructions and select the most appropriate in each case.
Be able to describe the auxiliary means of intervention.
Know the foundation and particularities of some of the techniques of intervention and vibration control in structures to reduce their vibratory level below the admissibility threshold.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. INTRODUCTION TO DYNAMIC CALCULATION OF STRUCTURES
1.2.- Examples and classification of dynamic loads
1.3.- Degrees of freedom in dynamic analysis
1.6.- Dynamic analysis as a structural project phase
Topic 2. SYSTEMS WITH 1 DEGREE OF FREEDOM
2.2.- 1 DOF model and equation of motion
Topic 3. SYSTEMS WITH SEVERAL DEGREES OF FREEDOM
3.2.- Equations of motion for systems with several DOFs
3.4.- Free vibration: natural frequencies and vibration modes
Topic 4. EXPERIMENTAL TECHNIQUES FOR VIBRATION MEASUREMENT
BLOCK 2. PATHOLOGY, INTERVENTION AND REINFORCEMENT OF REINFORCED CONCRETE STRUCTURES
Topic 5. PATHOLOGY OF REINFORCED CONCRETE STRUCTURES
teaching_methods: Practical sessions (laboratory): Problem-solving by the student using computer tools

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (laboratory practices/practical assignments, technical reports, oral presentations)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum global grade of 5 out of 10 is required. In the first and second calls, the final grade is calculated as 50% continuous assessment and 50% final exam. A minimum of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in the final exam; otherwise, the maximum overall grade will be 4.5 out of 10. Continuous assessment has no minimum mark and is recoverable in the second call. For the extraordinary end-of-studies call, the final exam accounts for 100% of the grade. Any fraudulent activity in assessment results in a grade of 0 for the activity or the entire call.
